name: OPA376AIDCKR
title: OPA376, OPA2376, OPA4376: low-noise, low-power precision CMOS op amps, rail-to-rail in and out
summary: Single, dual and quad CMOS operational amplifiers for 2.2 V to 5.5 V supplies, with inputs and outputs that swing to both rails. Production trim gives 5 µV typical and 25 µV maximum offset; noise is 7.5 nV/√Hz at 1 kHz and 0.8 µVPP from 0.1 Hz to 10 Hz. Gain bandwidth is 5.5 MHz on 760 µA per amplifier. They suit ADC drivers, audio, active filters and battery-powered sensor front ends.

circuits.title: Series output resistor for capacitive loads
circuits.description: A unity-gain follower whose output reaches the load through a small series resistor RS. The load is RL in parallel with CL. RS isolates the capacitance from the amplifier output, cutting ringing, while the feedback is still taken straight from the amplifier output pin.

circuits.title: Input current protection
circuits.description: A unity-gain follower with a 5 kΩ resistor in series with the noninverting input. When the input is driven past a supply rail, the resistor holds the current through the input clamp diodes to 10 mA or less.
notes: IOVERLOAD, the current into the input, is 10 mA max.

circuits.title: Basic single-supply connection (inverting, gain –10 V/V)
circuits.description: An inverting stage on one 5 V supply; R2/R1 sets the gain to –10 V/V. The noninverting input sits at VCM = 2.5 V, and the signal source rides on that level, so the output is centred on 2.5 V. VCM may be any value inside the input common-mode range. C1 bypasses the supply pin.

circuits.title: Second-order Butterworth 50 kHz low-pass filter
circuits.description: A multiple-feedback low-pass filter with a maximally flat response, cut-off at 50 kHz and –40 dB/decade beyond it. R1 feeds a node held by C1 to ground; R3 returns the output to that node and R2 carries it to the inverting input, which C2 ties to the output. The noninverting input and the source return sit at mid-supply, (V+)/2.

circuits.title: Driving an ADS8327 ADC
circuits.description: The amplifier is a unity-gain noninverting buffer between the signal and a 16-bit converter. Its output drives the ADC +IN through a 100 Ω resistor, with 1.2 nF from +IN to ground. The ADC –IN is grounded, and a REF5040 supplies the 4.096 V reference, bypassed by 100 nF. Everything runs from 5 V; C1 bypasses the amplifier supply.

circuits.title: Phantom-powered electret microphone
circuits.description: A microphone preamplifier powered over its own balanced cable. At the console end a 48 V phantom supply feeds both signal wires through 6.8 kΩ resistors; at the microphone end R8 and R9 (4.7 kΩ) and the 5.1 V zener D1 bring this down to a local supply, filtered by 100 Ω and 33 µF, that powers the OPA2376 and, through R1, the electret capsule. Amplifier A buffers the capsule; amplifier B inverts A's output with two 1 kΩ resistors around a bias taken from A's output through 10 kΩ and 10 µF. The two outputs drive the cable differentially through 33 µF and 100 Ω, for 6 dB of gain. At the console, 10 µF capacitors block the dc and an INA163, its gain set by RG from 0 dB to 80 dB, receives the balanced signal.

parts.note: electret microphone capsule; pin 1 output, pin 2 ground

notes: J1 and J2 are the two ends of one cable; pins 2 and 3 carry the differential audio and the phantom power together.

circuits.title: Speech band-pass data-acquisition system
circuits.description: An electret microphone, powered through R1, is ac coupled by C1 into a node biased at half the supply by R2 and R3. Amplifier A is a noninverting gain stage: R6 from its output to the inverting input, which R4 and R5 hold at half supply. Amplifier B, its noninverting input on the same biased node, is a multiple-feedback low-pass stage (R7, R8, R9, C2, C3). Its output drives the +IN of a 12-bit ADS7822 converter whose reference and supply come from V+. The pass band is 300 Hz to 3 kHz; the supply is 2.7 V to 5 V.

parts.note: 12-bit ADC; pins 1 VREF, 2 +IN, 3 –IN, 4 GND, 5 CS/SHDN, 6 DOUT, 7 DCLOCK, 8 V+

notes: The first stage carries the gain figure G = 100.

circuits.title: Typical application: second-order 25 kHz low-pass filter, gain –5 V/V
circuits.description: An infinite-gain multiple-feedback low-pass filter that inverts. R1 and R3 run in series from the input to the inverting input; C2 grounds their junction, R4 returns the output to it, and C5 ties the inverting input to the output. The noninverting input is grounded. The design targets an inverting gain of 5 V/V (R4/R1), a 25 kHz cut-off and a second-order Chebyshev response with 3 dB of peaking in the pass band.

operation.text: OPA376 is a single amplifier in SC70-5, SOT-23-5 or SOIC-8; OPA2376 a dual in SOIC-8, VSSOP-8 or DSBGA-8; OPA4376 a quad in TSSOP-14. All are CMOS, with inputs and outputs that reach both rails, 5.5 MHz bandwidth and about 760 µA per amplifier, and are specified from –40°C to 125°C.

One mode of operation only: the amplifier works from 2.2 V up to 5.5 V across its supply pins (±1.1 V to ±2.75 V split). Many limits hold over –40°C to 125°C; figures that move a lot with supply or temperature are given as typical curves.

Every amplifier has its offset trimmed in production by TI's e-trim, at wafer probe or final test. Because the trim comes in the last manufacturing steps, it also compensates shifts that molding causes. Typical offset is 5 µV.

The amplifier is stable at unity gain, and overdriving the input does not flip the output phase. Wired as a follower it can drive 250 pF of purely capacitive load directly, and higher gain raises that limit. Adding 10 Ω to 20 Ω between the output and a capacitive load damps ringing without hurting dc accuracy; if a resistor also loads the output, RS and RL divide the signal, giving a gain error proportional to RS / RL that is small at light output current.

The inputs work from 100 mV below V– to 100 mV above V+. Offset stays very low from V– up to about 1 V below V+, then rises. The CMRR limit applies for common-mode voltages between V– and 1.3 V below V+.

All pins have ESD protection; on the inputs and output it is mainly diodes that steer current to the supply pins. These diodes also survive input overdrive while the current stays at or under 10 mA. A resistor in series with the driven input limits that current, at the cost of thermal noise, so it is kept small where noise matters.
Fit a low-ESR 0.1 µF ceramic capacitor between each supply pin and ground, right next to the part. A single-supply design needs only the one on V+.

Use a ground plane, and keep analog and digital grounds physically apart, minding where ground current flows. Run input traces away from supply and output traces, crossing them at right angles if they must meet, and keep input traces short. Mount the feedback and gain resistors next to the inverting input to keep parasitic capacitance down. Surrounding sensitive traces with a guard ring held at low impedance cuts leakage from nearby nodes. Clean the board after assembly; after aqueous cleaning, bake it at 85°C for 30 minutes to drive moisture out of the packages.

The OPA2376YZD has a coating on its back, but light can still reach the die unless it is fully shielded. Bias current is specified in darkness; light raises the bias current and can raise offset, and fluorescent lighting can add hum. The end product's housing should shield the part from light.

The OPA2376YZD is a lead-free DSBGA: the bare die carries the solder bumps, without a plastic body, lead frame or bond wires, and it is soldered by ordinary surface-mount assembly without underfill. Its exact size is 1.150 mm × 2.188 mm. The top marking reads YMDCGLS: YMD is a year, month and day code, CGL identifies the OPA2376YZD, and S is for engineering use.
OPA376-Q1, OPA2376-Q1 and OPA4376-Q1 are AEC-Q100 qualified versions for automotive use.
